facts.text: Citrus Park earned its name when early settlers turned the desert floor into orange, grapefruit, and lemon groves thanks to the Salt River Project’s irrigation.
The community sits on the western edge of the Phoenix metropolitan area, about 25 miles west‑northwest of downtown Phoenix.
Perryville Road marks Citrus Park’s western boundary, yet it technically lies within Glendale’s city limits, hinting at future expansion possibilities.
Northern Avenue serves as the northern edge of Citrus Park, while Goodyear borders the south and Glendale the east.
Once dominated by citrus groves, the area has largely shifted to modern housing, yet it still acts as a gateway between the East Valley’s density and the western desert ranges.
The Waddell, Arizona post office provides mail services for Citrus Park residents, linking the community to the broader region.
